rows.claim: spoken audio reaches the model through its native pathway
rows.justified_interpretation: the processor expands a recording into placeholder tokens the model consumes, and no transcript is visible to the model
rows.notes: An input-path property. Unaffected by any endpoint question.

rows.claim: a candidate scoring path is valid for the audio condition
rows.justified_interpretation: the teacher-forced sum equals its own per-token terms, so the scorer is internally consistent
rows.notes: Validates the arithmetic of a scorer, not a scientific outcome.

rows.candidate_universe: six concepts, all named in the prompt
rows.claim: the model can read each concept out of each channel
rows.justified_interpretation: in a six-way forced choice whose options are listed in the prompt, the target concept's complete-sequence likelihood exceeded the other five
rows.notes: Narrower multiple-choice evidence. It gates admissibility and was never claimed as output; the wording 'can read out' is tightened to 'can select in a six-way forced choice'.

rows.candidate_universe: six concepts, all named in the prompt
rows.claim: capability accuracy per (concept, modality) clears 70%
rows.justified_interpretation: forced-choice accuracy over 8 samples per cell against a frozen threshold

rows.claim: the J-lens reproduces the model's own next token
rows.justified_interpretation: argmax over the model's complete next-token logits at the final prompt position — the same endpoint the corrected causal study uses
rows.notes: Unaffected. The lens work always measured the unrestricted endpoint; only the behavioral/causal work did not.

rows.claim: lens rank of the model's true next token beats its controls
rows.justified_interpretation: full-vocabulary rank statistics of the model's own argmax token under the lens, against noise and wrong-layer controls

rows.claim: the published lens confirms on held-out prompts
rows.justified_interpretation: agreement and rank of the model's actual final-layer top-1 token under the lens, over the full vocabulary

rows.candidate_universe: the retrieval gallery of held-out examples
rows.claim: J-space codes retrieve the matching cross-modal example
rows.justified_interpretation: activations of one modality are nearer their same-concept counterparts in another modality than a shuffled assignment is
rows.notes: Representational evidence. It never was an output claim, so the endpoint correction does not touch it.

rows.candidate_universe: the retrieval gallery under permuted labels
rows.claim: retrieval beats its shuffled-label control
rows.justified_interpretation: the retrieval statistic exceeds the 95th percentile of the same statistic under permuted labels

rows.claim: the multimodal pilot's causal cells moved the target
rows.justified_interpretation: the target answer's teacher-forced conditional log-probability moved in the intended direction relative to the clean run
rows.notes: `prediction_changed` is a restricted-candidate flip, not an output change. Genuine conditional-likelihood effect; not autonomous output.
prohibited_wording: the intervention changed the model's answer

rows.claim: the pilot's go/no-go criteria
rows.justified_interpretation: aggregate conditional-log-probability effects and their controls cleared frozen thresholds

rows.claim: text<->image transfer replicates on image-unique data
rows.justified_interpretation: controlled conditional-log-probability effects replicate on a population with one group per image

rows.claim: the causal effect is localized to particular layers
rows.justified_interpretation: the size of the conditional-log-probability effect differs between layers on paired inputs

rows.candidate_universe: six concepts, all named in the prompt
rows.claim: THREE_MODALITY_GO — cross-modal causal transfer including speech
rows.justified_interpretation: a source-derived J-space direction applied at one layer changed the target concept's conditional log-probability in the intended direction, against matched random, unrelated, zero and raw-residual controls, in both directions for at least one admissible concept
rows.notes: A genuine controlled conditional-likelihood effect. It is not evidence that any output token changed: the full vocabulary was never consulted. Corrected label: CONTROLLED_TARGET_LOGPROB_EFFECT plus FULL_VOCABULARY_NOT_EVALUATED.
prohibited_wording: the model said the swapped concept

rows.candidate_universe: six concepts, all named in the prompt
rows.claim: the capability-filtered v2 amendment's verdicts
rows.justified_interpretation: the same conditional-log-probability effects, re-read under the capability-admissibility rule; no measurement was recomputed

rows.claim: hidden-intermediate onset is localized among confirmed layers
rows.justified_interpretation: after the exchange the target answer outranked the one other supplied candidate more often than every matched control did
prohibited_wording: the model output the target answer

rows.claim: target answer becomes top-1 after the band swap
rows.justified_interpretation: `target_rank` is a rank among two supplied candidates; `prediction` is which of the two scored higher
rows.notes: The completed report measured whether `two` outranked `four`, not whether `two` was the global next-token argmax.
prohibited_wording: the target token became the model's top output

rows.claim: L33_L40_VALIDATED_BAND_FOLLOWUP_ALPHA2_SENSITIVITY_ONLY
rows.justified_interpretation: at alpha=2 only, the swap made the target answer the preferred one of two supplied candidates more often than every alpha=2-matched control; alpha=1 did not
rows.notes: Corrected label: RESTRICTED_CANDIDATE_PREFERENCE_GO at alpha=2 sensitivity only, plus FULL_VOCABULARY_NOT_EVALUATED. The numbers are unchanged; the `paper_comparable` field name is superseded by `restricted_candidate_preference`.

rows.claim: every physical band layer was patched on every trial
rows.justified_interpretation: the hooks fired at exactly the requested layers and at exactly the prompt positions the rule names

rows.claim: L33-L40 is the admissible band; L32 is excluded
rows.justified_interpretation: lens readout quality against noise, wrong-layer and coverage clauses, all computed over full-vocabulary rank statistics
rows.notes: Lens validation, not behaviour. Unaffected by the endpoint correction, and it is why the L33-L40 lenses may still be reused.

rows.claim: the layer has/has not converged to its output
rows.justified_interpretation: full-vocabulary logits produced by the model's own output head applied to an intermediate residual
rows.notes: This study already did what the causal studies did not: it read the whole distribution.

rows.claim: convergence classification per layer
rows.justified_interpretation: rates of full-vocabulary top-1 agreement and rank, against shuffled/permuted controls

rows.candidate_universe: the entire vocabulary; no candidate list is supplied
rows.claim: the target token is the global next-token argmax
rows.justified_interpretation: the complete next-token distribution at the final prompt position of the untouched prompt, with the intervention applied during that same forward pass
rows.notes: Not yet run against Gemma. Implementation only.

rows.claim: the model greedily writes the target answer
rows.justified_interpretation: a deterministic temperature-0 continuation of the prompt under the same intervention
rows.notes: Secondary demonstration. No verdict may rest on it.
prohibited_wording: greedy text alone establishes the causal claim

endpoint_trace_rule: every row was classified by reading the function that computes the field; no endpoint was inferred from report prose
